title: Semantic Tokens
summary: Add, inspect, edit, and report structured token occurrences through UI-led catalogue discovery, concrete target identity, and local relationship data.
content_html:
Semantic Tokens

Purpose

Make semantic tokens a coherent manage-mode Docs Viewer feature rather than a piece of source syntax an author must understand and maintain by hand.

Each accepted token family has:

  • one clearly named source-editor toolbar action and discovery workflow;
  • a modal that collects and validates the data needed to add it;
  • an Info-panel view that recognizes and edits an existing occurrence without changing its identity;
  • generated local relationship data and report behavior.

Catalogue is the first family. Its discovery modal helps an author choose among Work, Series, and Moment targets without deciding the target type before searching. Tag is a separate later family because it associates an abstraction rather than a catalogue entity.

Every later token family needs its own specification and delivery document.

Delivery is active only at the CT-P0 contract-fixture checkpoint. No production semantic-token behavior is approved until that checkpoint is reviewed and P1 is started explicitly.

Validation Boundary

The add-token modal is the only semantic validation gate. It requires a current lookup selection, validates the fields needed by that token kind, and inserts a well-formed string.

Source Markdown remains directly editable, so save and rebuild never validate the document's tokens. During rebuild, Docs Viewer opportunistically projects a recognized string only when its configured lookup supplies a workable link. If the string is malformed, unsupported, or unresolved, the builder leaves it as ordinary source text and emits no semantic link or usage relationship. It does not fail or warn merely because token-like text cannot be resolved.

Repair belongs to the existing manage-only Docs Broken Links report. Its read-only audit independently scans for semantic-token link failures, then opens the owning source document so the author can remove the broken occurrence and add the correct target through the modal. This diagnostic workflow does not turn save or rebuild into validation.

Feature Boundary

Semantic tokens are an integrated Docs Viewer capability:

  • source-editor core continues to own the Markdown buffer, selection, dirty state, save, rebuild, and ordinary media insertion;
  • the semantic-token layer contributes family-specific actions, modals, Info views, parsing, a token-definition registry, configured target projections, a derived usage index, and reports;
  • canonical target records remain with their domain owners.

Generic core has no token-definition registry. Core Add image and Add file save the media and insert ordinary Markdown links; they do not wrap those links in semantic tokens.

The feature is manage-only. It adds no public token UI, token-definition registry, usage index, token-aware runtime, or report.

If a later document or report consumer is approved for a public scope, its builder packages only successfully resolved tokens and their exact browser-safe fields into a focused published payload. The public reader must not resolve tokens against canonical source, the manage target lookup, or the manage usage index at runtime. That projection is a separate feature and delivery contract.

Documents

  • Concept defines the user outcome, mental model, and invariants.
  • Source Editor UI defines addition, caret recognition, highlighting, Info-panel editing, and removal.
  • Architecture derives token syntax, token-definition configuration, target projections, usage data, ownership, generated files, and wiring from the UI workflow.
  • Catalogue Token Delivery delivers the first complete token family.

Design Gate

Design proceeds from the authoring decision to its representation:

source-editor workflow
    -> token syntax
    -> family and target data structure
    -> integration and refactoring decisions
    -> Catalogue token delivery

The UI establishes when the author chooses meaning and which information helps that choice. The syntax then records the selected concrete identity. The data structure supplies discovery, configured projections, and usage data for that workflow. If required data cannot be entered, explained, inspected, or edited through the modal and Info view, neither syntax nor token-kind definition is ready.

Internal Order

  1. Accept the Source Editor UI workflow.
  2. Derive and accept the token syntax from that workflow.
  3. Accept the family/target data structure and integration architecture.
  4. Promote and implement the Catalogue Token Delivery as one vertical slice.
  5. Write a separate specification and delivery before adding another family.
